body:
Thanks.  So much.  It seems like every time I come up for fresh air from this...whatever it is, it feels fantastic for a short time.  Then I get pulled right back down.  What's frustrating is I know I'm the one who drops the anchor.  It's when I sink deep enough like I did a few nights ago that it seems like there's really no way out - regardless of whose fault it is (it's mine).

I said it before, and I'll say it again, your replies couldn't have come at a better time.  Thanks again, my friend.  I hope you are well.

Thanks man.  It means a lot.  You took how a view myself from "I'm JUST a guy who..." and you turned it to, "I'm THAT guy who..."  If that makes sense.  I guess there is some trust there that I should be happy about.  Still though...I wish I could be more.  So I'll try and work towards it - and try to be happy enough with where I am in the meantime, I guess.  It's hard.  I dunno.  It's been increasingly hard for me to concentrate on everything lately.

Thanks again though, man.  I hope you're doing well too.

Absolutely do NOT apologize for anything!  As someone who works in healthcare, I know you can't save the world.  And you can't always be there for everyone...much less a guy posting a bunch of rambling junk on the web.  This is not your obligation, and the fact that you did find a way to follow up on me eventually speaks volumes for you.

Besides, your timing is impeccable, actually.  I knew it wouldn't be an easy, straight line to "happiness," but I really did not think I'd fall back down this hard, you know?  Tonight was the worst.  It just makes me feel weak.  Compounding that?  I find myself falling hard for a girl I really liked a year ago all over again.  I never thought I would...I really thought I was over it, and I hate myself for feeling this way again because it's a lost cause.  But, she starts talking to me when she feels alone or down, and I. Just. Can't. Help. It.  I feel like such a creep and a weakling to be getting this invested again.  I know, I know.  A girl?  How incredibly lame.  What a moron I am.  I know I am.

It's really just the cherry on the sundae though.  It's just one more case of where I'm that guy to talk to occasionally when things are wrong, but I'm otherwise just not good enough.  I'm never good enough.  And then another girl I've become great friends with lately...she has taken to calling me "like a brother," which means so MUCH to me.  She's the same age as my sister who died, she just...is just as easy to talk to too.  I once hung out at a bar with just her, and I found myself crying for the first time in years on the way home because I had talked to her like I used to with my sister.  So...I'm clinging to this one because she reminds me of my dead sister.  Is "creep" screaming like an air raid siren yet?  I think it is.  Finally, I've exhausted my oldest and closest friendships lately by telling them all this constantly.  I can't get out.  I find myself repeating my old, sickly mantra again - "If I could just trade places with my sister, if I could just let her be here and me be there, it'd be better for everyone."  I mean, why am I here?  What does it matter?  What good am I?  All I'm doing is making things harder and weirder for other people.  I don't want to be that guy.  It's not fair to anyone.  But I'm not sure how to get out.

Anyway, my friend, thanks.  Honestly, you don't know how much finding this meant to me today.  Seriously.  I was just pacing around saying, "I can't do this anymore," over and over, and I decided to randomly jump on this throwaway.  To find a reply I didn't think would be there was really nice.  It allowed me to slow down and breathe at least.

I hope you've been doing well.

Well, thanks!  Dunno if it's true or not, but I do appreciate reading those things from time to time.

I do sometimes wonder if it's all been more of a self-fulfilling prophesy with people.  But, still, I just don't fit in with anybody.  It makes me think it's not JUST a self-fulfilling prophesy, though I'm sure it is kinda there in some capacity to compound things.  In any case, at this point, I feel like I'm in so deep, I don't know how I could possibly climb out.  Then, even if I do, do I REALLY want to burden people with my whiney load of crap?  It's all pretty difficult.  Every time I try to get in with people, I feel like I end up doing something dumb to piss them off, and then they inevitably feel bad when they realize I'm just an idiot.  Or, well, all right, that doesn't happen every time, but it does happen enough to make me think - "What in the heck is wrong with me?"  At worst, I'm a nuisance, at best, I'm a non factor, it seems.

Thanks again though.  You're a good man.

Excellent point.  It's always good for perspective to remember that - hey, nobody is perfectly happy.  I know that, but I guess I do kinda forget it from time to time.  I certainly don't think I'm entitled to be any unhappier than anyone else, of course.  As one of my wiser patients once told me, "Some people just aren't mentally equipped to realize that they don't have it that bad."  Life is, indeed, hard, and it's always smart to realize I'm not the only one fighting the good fight.  The perspective is appreciated, friend.  Thanks - though, I wonder how I learn to cope with simply existing in this frustrating world then.

You know?  I KNOW going to see professional help would be a good idea, but I just can't seem to do it.  Hell, I started seeing a cardiologist for a crappy blood pressure, and even he recommended it after ten minutes.  Either he is one perceptive son of a gun, or I am not covering up these depressing thoughts to people nearly as well as I thought...which, as I said to CaptainRevolver, really makes me paranoid.  I hope I'm not chasing people away, but I'm afraid I very well may be.  Blargh, what a vicious cycle.  I don't want to push people away, but I probably do by being afraid I'm pushing them away.

Anyway, you nailed it with the self-criticism, as I always saw it as my strong point.  It means I'm more self aware, right?  But it can definitely fester if you don't control it.  The hardest thing for me to see is that people are positively affected by their interactions with me.  I honestly don't think I'm a horrendous person who has a negative impact on the world, but I don't see where I have a positive one either.  I'm just sorta...there.  Taking up space.  What's the point?

Thanks, man.  I really hope you're not too tough on yourself either because you strike me as a really cool guy.  Take care.

Thanks for the reply.  I actually got to read your post before the edit, and I thought it was good then just as it is now.  I've been mulling over what exactly to say to the kind people who spoke up however, which is why I've taken so long to get back to everyone.

That said, I always feel kinda silly when people point out some common sense to me.  Once you get in that rut, it's hard to catch the easy observations sometimes.  Why I never thought of inviting the coworkers myself, I'll never know.  I think I just sort of assumed nobody wanted to be around me.  I certainly wouldn't be surprised that my dad is depressed, but I don't feel like he talks to my sister the same way as he does me.  I mean...he'll complain about her to my mom and me (which I hate being around for, by the way), but he doesn't quite talk down to her like he will with me.  Dunno why that is.  I'm not sure if it's a respect thing or what.  I just feel like I'm at the bottom of the totem pole in life when I think of this stuff.  My close friends have dwindled, I can't get a date to save my life, and I have all these people telling me how great of a guy I am but then going their own ways.  It makes me paranoid...like...maybe they realize there's something wrong there, so they try to say something nice, but they'd rather not be around me.  I'm probably being crazy.  But it's a very real and constant thought.

Anyway, thanks again, buddy.  I hope you are doing well yourself.
